publishedWalks.title: The Highgate Village Self-Guided Walk — Richard Jones
stories: Advertises Dickens family lodgings, pub rituals, literary house identifications, Coleridge and piped water. These are provider claims, not independently verified history. Locator: lines 61–123. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

Several associations are expressly speculative or attributed; preserve those qualifications rather than converting them into facts. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

publishedWalks.title: Lady’s Beautiful Highgate Walk and Map — A Lady in London
themes: Linear walk advertised as two to three hours, not a Highgate station loop
stories: Primarily a place-discovery guide rather than a historical anecdote tour; cemetery admission is an optional diversion. Locators: lines 26–91. ([aladyinlondon.com](https://www.aladyinlondon.com/2022/09/highgate-walk.html))

publishedWalks.title: Highgate Village — a place apart — London Walks
stops: Highgate station ticket hall: advertised meeting point
Village lanes and Georgian houses: individual stops unspecified
Highgate Cemetery and Kenwood House: explicitly post-walk options, not confirmed tour stops
stories: Advertising names Coleridge, Dickens, Betjeman, Cromwell, Nell Gwyn and others without supplying the individual stories or their locations. Locators: lines 78–92; do not infer an itinerary from the names. ([walks.com](https://www.walks.com/our-walks/highgate-village-a-place-apart))

publishedWalks.title: Historic walk in Highgate Wood — City of London
stops: Information Hut by the café: confirmed advertised start
Further numbered stops: unknown because the linked leaflet failed to load
themes: Leaflet credited to local historian Michael Hammerson
stories: The landing page does not disclose individual historical stories. Updated October 29, 2024; locator: lines 25–29. ([cityoflondon.gov.uk](https://www.cityoflondon.gov.uk/things-to-do/green-spaces/highgate-wood/historic-walk-in-highgate-wood))

publishedWalks.title: Highgate North Hill / North Hill Challenge — Highgate Society, Northern Heights Circuit
stops: North Hill–Archway Road junction: advertised finish
themes: 34 buildings arranged by approximate construction chronology
Short architectural walk intended to combine with other circuit sections
stories: Explains how façades can conceal rebuilding, how housing forms changed, and contrasts older houses, council housing and modernist flats. Locators: PDF pages 1–2, 11 and 14–15. Publication date not established. ([highgatesociety.com](https://www.highgatesociety.com/media/docs/North%20Hill%20descriptions.pdf))

candidates.name: Highgate Underground station public exterior
candidates.why: Mandatory start and return anchor, not yet a historical storytelling stop. For newcomers, use it to establish orientation and the relationship between station and village. Exact exit and safe exterior standing point remain unverified.

candidates.name: Highpoint, North Hill
candidates.why: Candidate for discovering modernist housing rather than assuming Highgate is entirely Georgian. The Society identifies Lubetkin and Tecton and dates the two buildings to 1935 and 1938; verify historical claims independently. Proposed anchor: public pavement, not entrance canopy or private gardens. PDF page 14. ([highgatesociety.com](https://www.highgatesociety.com/media/docs/North%20Hill%20descriptions.pdf))

candidates.name: 41 North Hill
candidates.why: A compact lesson in distinguishing a building’s age from its visible façade. The Society attributes sixteenth-century dating to a plaque and qualifies the later remodelling. Proposed anchor: public pavement opposite, subject to safe sightline verification. PDF page 2. ([highgatesociety.com](https://www.highgatesociety.com/media/docs/North%20Hill%20descriptions.pdf))

candidates.name: 99 North Hill and Kenwood estate housing
candidates.why: Potential social-housing counterpoint to grand houses. The Society attributes these homes to Hornsey Council around 1902. Investigate that local proposition without adopting its broad legislative claim. Proposed anchor: public pavement; northern detour must earn its measured walking cost. PDF page 11. ([highgatesociety.com](https://www.highgatesociety.com/media/docs/North%20Hill%20descriptions.pdf))

candidates.name: The Gatehouse exterior
candidates.why: Explore the village-name and toll-gate proposition advertised by Jones; distinguish the earlier site from the present building. Proposed anchor: pavement outside, without requiring a purchase or entry. Lines 74–77. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: Pond Square
candidates.why: Discover an absent landscape feature through the surviving place-name. Jones advertises pond infilling in 1864; independently verify it. Proposed anchor: public square, exact standing point unresolved. Lines 80–84. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: Highgate Literary and Scientific Institution, 11 South Grove
candidates.why: Potential discovery: village knowledge-sharing rather than another famous resident. Jones advertises an 1839 foundation. Proposed anchor: public pavement facing the façade; no interior access assumed. Lines 93–97. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: St Michael’s Church exterior
candidates.why: Candidate for examining how literary memory moves: Jones advertises Coleridge’s reinterment here. Proposed anchor: public street with spire view; churchyard access and interior grave visibility are not assumed. Lines 100–104. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: 3 The Grove, Coleridge-associated house
candidates.why: A residence-based literary candidate, potentially preferable to repeating the burial story. Jones advertises a commemorative plaque and residence with Gillman. Proposed anchor: public lane, respecting residential privacy. Specific visitor anecdotes need independent checking. Lines 122–124. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: Waterlow Park and Lauderdale House exterior
candidates.why: Potential green-space and civic-life contrast to residential streets. The published guide includes the house-side park entrance and city views, but supplies little historical evidence. Proposed anchor: public park path with exterior view; current opening hours and chosen gate need verification. Lines 52–57. ([aladyinlondon.com](https://www.aladyinlondon.com/2022/09/highgate-walk.html))

candidates.name: Highgate Cemetery entrances on Swain’s Lane
candidates.why: Consider a cemetery-history stop that works entirely outside the admission boundary. Published walks advertise the cemetery, but this proposal must not depend on grave visibility or entry. Proposed anchor: public pavement away from entrance queues; safe space and exterior sightlines unresolved. ([aladyinlondon.com](https://www.aladyinlondon.com/2022/09/highgate-walk.html))

candidates.name: Highgate Wood entrance or nearby public path
candidates.why: Woodland history offers a different subject from celebrity residences. The City advertises a dedicated historic walk, but its detailed leaflet was unavailable; no specific woodland anecdote is yet supported. Proposed anchor: verified public entrance or path, not automatically the café. Potential northern alternative, not an obligatory addition. ([cityoflondon.gov.uk](https://www.cityoflondon.gov.uk/things-to-do/green-spaces/highgate-wood/historic-walk-in-highgate-wood))

gaps: Status: request 1/5 is a fresh survey and candidate proposal only. Five published guides were catalogued, one incompletely. No route has been accepted, no script written, and no output published.

Input revision retained: schemaVersion 1; brief ID highgate-sol61-v7; mapId hampstead-0abcc26a600e0718; map path local-data/generation-map-data/highgate-261006.json; SHA-256 25ff2e0466dbe4a8250c2dcc8cebde297cb752c3415675ea547a73315c732275. The local file was not accessible or independently hashed in this tool context.

Constraints retained: Highgate Underground public exterior start and finish; 3600-second target; daytime public exterior access; ordinary hills and steps allowed; no paid admission; generation allowance 90 minutes; direct paid ceiling USD 0; voice local Kokoro George; model gpt-6.1-sol; effort medium.

Evidence limitation: no read_page tool was available. Hosted web.open outputs were read for catalogue paraphrases and locators, but no exact source passages are returned or represented as compliant read_page evidence. Candidate history remains provisional until the required evidence capture is available.

Source provenance: provider pages establish advertised content, not the truth of every historical assertion. Source families are commercial guide, travel blog, tour operator, local authority and local society. No open reuse licence was established; retain links and factual paraphrases only, and do not reuse authored narration or images.

Failed attempts: the City of London’s linked Highgate Wood leaflet returned an internal error. One tool invocation failed JSON parsing before execution and was corrected. No detailed woodland stop list or story was recovered.

Negative findings: London Walks does not publish a complete stop-by-stop itinerary; its cemetery and Kenwood suggestions are explicitly post-walk options. The woodland landing page supplies a start and duration but no individual stories. The A Lady in London route ends at Tufnell Park and cannot be adopted as the required loop.

Questions changing selection: should the preferred balance be village institutions and public landscape, or a northern architectural/woodland loop? Can cemetery history earn an exterior-only stop without implying that famous graves are visible? These choices should be resolved by fresh leg measurements and supported local detail, not by adding every candidate.

Geometry and access unknown: no map-query or routing tools were available, and no per-job map receipts, offlineMap bounds object or previousRouting leg measurements were supplied. No query radius was requested. The stated OSM extract timestamp is October 6, 2026 at 20:21:06Z; features alone would not establish current access.

Duration unresolved: no measured walking legs, crossing/hill allowances or rendered audio exist. At 80 seconds per stop, 10 stops require 41 minutes 40 seconds of walking and other allowances to reach 55 minutes; 12 require 39 minutes. Neither is a route estimate, and the candidate list must not be treated as a selected itinerary.

Usage: four successful hosted-web calls, containing two searches, eight opens, one click and two finds; one additional malformed invocation failed before execution. One research context was used. No purchases, paid admission, rendering or other spending were initiated. Tool-provider charges, token usage and elapsed wall-clock time are unknown because no usage or timer receipt was exposed.

Unavailable project controls: docs/ISSUES.md and the referenced issue records were not supplied and could not be inspected. No prior project research, candidates, geometry or scripts were used. No human listening, field visit or eyewitness observation is claimed.

Recommended next action: retain this survey and stable candidate IDs; provide compliant read_page evidence capture and fresh bounded map/routing tools. Compare compact village and northern alternatives, including the station return, then research only the candidates and named blockers needed for selection. After acceptance, verify standing points, directions and conservative duration; render original narration and use actual audio length for the final 55–65-minute estimate. Playback coverage, saved map, AI provenance and manual navigation/audio fallback remain later verification tasks.
